I have been working this land since I was a young man. My father farmed before me, and I have learned what this soil needs through decades of trial. My 13.1 mu grows wheat in the cold months and maize in the hot months — the same rotation I have done for most of my life. With just two of us in the house now, and my knees not what they were, I cannot spend extra days on heavy work. I know what gives me a reliable harvest.

For **wheat**, I will plant in early October after rotary tilling the field. I will buy improved variety seeds from the county supply cooperative — the local-adapted varieties like Jimai or Shixin types that the other villagers here also use. They sprout well in our soil. I will apply compound base fertilizer before planting, then topdress with urea at the jointing stage. My well gives me water, so I will irrigate four times: the winter water in November to protect roots from freezing, then at jointing, heading, and grain filling. I will spray herbicide once in spring and do one more pass for disease if the weather is wet. Rotary tillage is enough — I cannot manage a full plough anymore.

For **maize**, I will plant right after the wheat harvest in mid-June. I have been buying hybrid seeds —郑单958 type — for over twenty years. The yields are simply better. I will not till deeply, just direct seed into the wheat stubble with rotary preparation. Maize in summer heat needs more nitrogen, so I push that up. I will irrigate at germination if it is dry, then at jointing and tasseling. Two or three pesticide passes — herbicide early, then one for borers.

I expect around 450 jin per mu from wheat and 550 jin per mu from maize. Enough for the household and some to sell.
